exposure: time interval between the birth of the first and second twin greater than 15 minutes
twin to twin delivery time interval
birth weight discordance of 25% or more
cohort: 183 parturients carrying twin pregnancies at the department of Obstetrics-Gynecology in Mahmoud Matri Hospital (Ariana) over a period of 9 years (January 1, 2001, to December 31, 2009)
finding: A gestational age ≤ 34 weeks, a low birth weight ≤ 1500g, and a twin-to-twin delivery time interval ≥ 15 minutes were factors that significantly influenced the Apgar score at 1 and 5 minutes and were responsible for more neonatal distress and transfer to pediatrics.
mod_finding: The different modes of delivery and the type of presentation of the second twin did not significantly alter the rate of neonatal respiratory distress or transfer to pediatrics.
